correctness.rationale: Writing \(n=2^a m\) with \(m\) odd partitions every divisor uniquely as \(2^jd\), giving the exact factorization \(E_s(n)=\sigma_s(m)(\sum_{j=1}^a2^{js}-1)\). The sign classification follows from a monotone geometric sum. For \(s<0\), the divisor-swapped summatory series has absolutely convergent main coefficient \((2^s-1)\zeta(1-s)\), and the tail plus floor error is \(o(x)\). The verifier independently checks the exact divisor formula and representative summatory convergence.

value.rationale: The claim directly answers a named research problem for the first nontrivial modulus \(q=2\), rather than an arbitrary slice. It gives a complete all-real-parameter pointwise phase transition at \(s=-1\), exact natural densities in the intermediate regime, and a contrasting linear cumulative bias for every \(s<0\). This explains both local oscillation and global bias in the same object.
